title: 회사에서 말하기: 할수록 · 오듯이 · 아시다시피
objective: By the end, you can tell -을수록, -듯이 and -다시피 apart and use them correctly in sentences. You can also choose the right form for ㄹ stems, ㅂ-irregular stems and polite speech.
summary: This worksheet compares three endings: -을수록 (the more…, the more…), -듯이 (like, just as) and -다시피 (as you know or see).

task.title: Use the right ending
task.line: Fill in the blanks, combine the sentences, or choose the form that fits each sentence.

forms.when: The stem ends in a vowel. Add ㄹ to the stem and then 수록 (배우다 → 배울수록). If the stem already ends in ㄹ, use -수록 instead.
forms.exampleMeaning: The more I learn Korean, the more fun it is.

forms.when: The stem already ends in the final consonant ㄹ. The ㄹ stays as it is, so add only -수록 (살다 → 살수록). Do not add another ㄹ or 을.
forms.example: 이 동네는 오래 살수록 정이 들어요.
forms.exampleMeaning: The longer you live in this neighborhood, the more attached you get.

forms.when: The stem ends in a consonant (not ㄹ).
forms.exampleMeaning: The more people there are, the longer the line.

forms.when: Say the same verb twice to make 'more and more' stronger.
forms.means: the more (you do it), the more …
forms.exampleMeaning: The more I look at this puppy, the cuter it gets.

forms.when: Add it to any verb stem. It works the same after a vowel or a consonant.
forms.exampleMeaning: Sweat is pouring down like rain.

forms.when: Use it for something that already happened or was already said.
forms.exampleMeaning: As I said yesterday, the meeting starts at 3.

forms.when: Use it mainly with 알다, 보다, 듣다 and 느끼다. Use -(으)시다시피 when you speak politely to the listener. 듣다 is ㄷ-irregular, so it becomes 들으시다시피 / 들으셨다시피 in polite speech. Also, -다시피 하다 means 'almost doing' (e.g. 거의 살다시피 하다).
forms.means: as you know / as you can see
forms.exampleMeaning: As you know, next week is a long holiday.

watchOut: 살을수록 (X) → 살수록 (O): If the stem ends in ㄹ, add only -수록. Another example: 길다 → 길수록.
춥을수록 (X) → 추울수록 (O): In ㅂ-irregular stems, ㅂ changes to 우.
먹었을수록 (X) → 먹을수록 (O): Do not put a past-tense ending before -을수록.
비가 오다시피 (X) → 비가 오듯이 (O): -다시피 means 'as you know/see' and goes with verbs like 알다 and 보다. To say 'like', use -듯이.
사장님, 알다시피 (X) → 사장님, 아시다시피 (O): When you speak to someone older or senior, add -시-.
exercises: Fill in the blank with -을수록: 이 소설은 ____ 더 슬퍼져요. (읽다)
Fill in the blanks with the right form of -ㄹ수록/-을수록/-수록: ① 집이 회사에서 ____ 출퇴근이 힘들어요. (멀다) ② 날씨가 ____ 물을 많이 마셔야 해요. (덥다)
Combine the two sentences with -(으)면 -을수록, repeating the same verb: 이 일을 해요. / 쉬워져요.
Choose the right form: ① 땀이 비 (오듯이 / 오다시피) 흘러요. ② 손님, (보시다시피 / 보실수록) 방이 아주 넓어요.
Fill in the blank with the past form of -듯이 (use 말하다, not -다시피): 지난주에 제가 ____ 내일은 사무실 청소가 있어요. (말하다)
You are talking to your manager. Choose the right form: 부장님, (알다시피 / 아시다시피) 이번 달은 주문이 많아요.
